Fed's Collins says gradual rate hikes best to manage economic risks

A number of Fed officials have said a more measured pace of rate increases allows the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs.

BOSTON: Fed eral Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said on Saturday (Nov 14) she supported a steady pace of modest interest rate increases because that path of action better managed economic uncertainties. When it comes to moving monetary policy to a tighter footing, "a steady, gradual path seems appropriate to me at the moment. But I'm open-minded," Collins told reporters at a conference held by her bank on housing issues in Boston. “I do see the risks as two-sided on the real side of the economy," Collins said, with inflation high and its gains broadening throughout the economy, while the job market was stable with the potential to accelerate. At the same time, there are the ongoing risks of more shocks hitting the economy, Collins said. Furthermore, “it's possible that the rise in medium to longer term rates that we've seen since the beginning of the year may actually weigh on demand more than I'm thinking,” and serve as another source of restraint on economic activity, she said.

RATE INCREASES IN DECEMBER, JANUARY SEEN The Fed last raised rates in September, and it is widely expected to lift its current 3.75 percent to 4 percent interest rate target range by a quarter percentage point at the December 8-9 monetary policy meeting, following that with another increase in January. Most Fed officials have signalled support for steady and small increases to help lower inflation, but last week's price data and the comments of Fed Governor Christopher Waller have suggested some on the Fed may want a bigger increase next month. A number of Fed officials have said a more measured pace of rate increases allows the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs. Collins cautioned that her expectation that the Fed can move gradually "doesn't necessarily mean a particular cadence." She also reiterated that the data flow from recent months has shifted where the Fed could end up in its current tightening cycle. “I do think that the price data we've seen over the past three months, and the labor market on a stronger footing, does make me think that the path of policy rates over the, you know, next year might be a bit higher than I had thought a couple of months ago,” Collins said.

Source: Reuters/fs

MADRID, Nov 14 : England manager Thomas Tuchel does not expect racist abuse during Sunday's Nations League clash with Spain but said his players would be reminded of anti-racism protocols, prompting a terse response from Spain coach Luis de la Fuente. England face the world champions in Madrid with top spot in their Nations League group at stake, returning to the Spanish capital for the first time since a 2004 friendly in which Black England players, including Ashley Cole and Shaun Wright-Phillips, were subjected to racist abuse from the crowd. England midfielder Declan Rice said the squad knew exactly how to respond if racism occurred. "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro, Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place we followed," Rice told reporters on Saturday. "We came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"I'm not expecting any of that. This is a beautiful city, great stadium, the players we're playing against we have a lot of respect for. It's set up to be a really good evening and hopefully not a negative one." The issue gained traction after Spain were fined $20,000 following anti-Muslim chants by supporters during a match against Egypt in Barcelona in March. Spain must also play their next home friendly with a reduced-capacity crowd as part of the punishment. RACISM NOT A PROBLEM IN SPAIN De la Fuente rejected any suggestion that racism was a problem in Spain. "What I can tell you, and you can pass this on to Thomas, is that there is no racism in Spain. That's how strongly I feel about it," De la Fuente said. "There is no racism. Just as in England, there is no racism in Spain. None of us are racist." Tuchel bristled when told of De la Fuente's remarks, accusing sections of the Spanish media of misrepresenting his comments. "I was polite enough to (answer) a question from your colleagues, and you run and ask the other coach and tell him that I talk about racism in Spain," Tuchel said. "I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question about what happens. I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on earth." James Trafford will start in goal for England on Saturday, said Tuchel, who added that everyone was fit to play including Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence who have recovered from injury.

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Nov 14 : England winger Will Joseph scored a record-equalling five tries to lead his side to a runaway 78-15 Nations Championship win over Japan at Twickenham on Saturday. Joseph was making only his second appearance for England, more than four years after his debut, and started his return with a try from his first touch inside the opening 65 seconds before adding three more in the first 25 minutes. The 24-year-old scored a fifth with an intercept after the interval to equal the record set by Rory Underwood in 1989 and matched by Josh Lewsey in 2003 and Henry Arundell at the last World Cup. England ran in 13 tries in a record score against Japan, and in the new Nations Championship competition.

There were also scores for Freddie Steward, Ellis Genge, Cadan Murley and Ben Earl in an eight-try spree in the first half and for George Martin, Ben Curry, Marcus Smith and Greg Fisilau after the break. George Ford converted three tries and kicked a penalty and Henry Slade added two conversions. Warner Dearns and Helu Opeti claimed Japan’s tries, the first converted by Naoto Saito, who also put over a penalty. Japan coach Eddie Jones, who spent seven years in charge of England, had promised he would try to create chaos but his game plan was dismantled by England's early try and Japan lock Harry Hockings getting sent to the sin bin for an illegal tackle. His early yellow card was upgraded to a 20-minute red, and England took full advantage. "I loved every minute of that and a joy to be part of. It was a pretty perfect day," Joseph said. There was no let-up as the hosts turned the screws with powerful carrying through the middle, strong rucking and bruising tackling as they moved into second spot in the Northern Hemisphere standings. "There were a lot of things to be pleased about, with wonderful tries from various sources," England coach Steve Borthwick said. (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

KYIV: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy escalated his criticism of SpaceX on Saturday (Nov 14), saying speed restrictions on its military-grade Starshield satellite terminals had dangerous political implications and undermined critical air defences. Zelenskyy said Starshield terminals operating in temporarily Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine had been limited to a maximum speed of 161 kph for the past five days, hampering Ukraine's military capabilities. The Ukrainian Defence Ministry has raised the issue with SpaceX at the institutional level, Zelenskyy said. "The restrictions have now been in place for five days. They say it is some kind of technical issue. We do not believe that is the case," Zelenskyy told reporters in remarks released by his office on Saturday.

"If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognising the temporarily occupied territories as not ours. And that is why I believe we have the right to raise this issue and restore the speed – so that there are no restrictions at all." Zelenskyy said the speed restrictions made it more difficult for Ukrainian air defence units to intercept Russian jet-powered drones and made Ukrainian cities more vulnerable. He said he had ordered his top military and foreign ministry officials to address the issue and seek clarification. SpaceX has pushed back against the allegations, denying that it introduced new restrictions or made any changes to its satellite operations. It is the second such outage in recent weeks. In mid-October, Ukrainian officials said that SpaceX limited the speed of Starlink and its Starshield communication systems to about 160 kph amid tensions with US President Donald Trump's administration over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. Service was then restored on Oct 24.

CARDIFF, Nov 14 : Wales hailed a heroic performance as they scored five tries and defended superbly to beat New Zealand 35-28 on Saturday and end a 73-year wait for a win over the All Blacks. The shock Nations Championship triumph was a massive fillip for the game in Wales, which had been reeling after a record-breaking run of 18 successive defeats following the last World Cup. Although they won three of their last five tests, Wales had mustered only five victories in 32 internationals over the last three years. "The effort that the players and staff have put in over the last 15 months or so, they got what they deserved today. It was an unbelievable performance from the boys," Wales coach Steve Tandy said.

"We spoke about attacking, building the performance and being brave and I thought the boys were, probably over brave before halftime, but they had intent to go after the game. "When New Zealand were coming back at halftime it would be easy to doubt yourselves, but I thought the last couple of minutes they looked really composed." Captain Dewi Lake said not having to face up to reporters after another defeat made a pleasant change. "We got asked a lot of questions last week about performance. We had a lot of tough conversations. It's nothing this group doesn't deserve. Steve talks about performance a lot. That's why when you get it right, the result takes care of itself." Wales beat Japan 28-21 last weekend in a far from convincing performance. "I'm always proud of this group. I'm not proud of this group because we've beaten New Zealand. I'm proud of the tough times and the good times they've been through," Lake said. "Of course, we believed we could do it. Sometimes we can say that and it's a passing comment for people at home. But we meant this."

WASHINGTON: Airlines canceled 4,500 US flights and delayed 4,400 more on Saturday (Nov 14) as the United States struggled to recover from the longest nationwide shutdown of flights since the Sep 11 2001 attacks . Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford apologized for the disruption, saying the system was stable and he expected airline operations to largely return to normal by late Sunday. The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours due to a massive communications failure, which forced airlines to cancel nearly 10,000 flights and delay more than 7,000 others on Friday in one of the worst travel days in US history. The issue prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday and federal agencies to scramble to determine if it was a cyberattack. Instead, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday that FAA contractor L3Harris' LHX.N installation of at least one new router at a remote facility triggered the disruption.

We haven't determined what the fault was," Duffy said at a press conference. L3Harris did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Its shares last traded down about four percent after hours on Friday.

OVERLOADED COMMUNICATIONS CENTRES The issue led to data overloading other communications centres. "We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was (it) gave us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar," Duffy added. The issue affected communications at 17 of 22 en route centres, the FAA facilities that control aircraft during the cruise portion of a flight, across the country. Bedford said the FAA ordered the ground stop in case a centre lost total communications. "No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost," Bedford added. The FAA said it was doing additional testing with L3Harris to see if there are any additional risks. Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and American Airlines all canceled about 20 percent of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue canceled 40 percent. Airlines have issued travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook flights for later dates without cost. Though the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday evening, the disruption for passengers was far from over, with tens of thousands of people stranded in airports. Airlines were trying to get flight crews and other personnel in position to resume flights. The disruption stranded some college football teams on Friday before games scheduled for Saturday. The FAA issued the ground stop because of an outage that appeared to affect a network that handles critical radio frequencies used by air traffic controllers to communicate with pilots, according to two airline officials. L3Harris oversees the network.

United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy takes questions as US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin looks on in the James S Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House in Washington DC, Nov 13 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Elizabeth Frantz)

FUNDS SOUGHT TO FIX 'EMERGENCY' Friday's disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers. Duffy called on Friday for US$50 billion in funding to upgrade air traffic control systems, up from his earlier request of US$30 billion. "This is an emergency," he said. Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when air traffic control centers experienced instability in radar and communications systems. Because the FAA was responsible for passenger delays, airlines are not required to provide compensation. The only other nationwide ground stop since the Sep 11 attacks came in Jan 2023, when the FAA halted domestic departures for about 90 minutes, disrupting about 11,000 flights.

Source: Reuters/fs

CARDIFF, Nov 14 : Wales ended a 73-year winless sequence against New Zealand with a stunning 35-28 victory in the Nations Championship on Saturday. Wales, who last overcame the All Blacks in 1953 and have endured a dismal recent run, outscored the visitors five tries to four and produced a defensive performance for the ages to end a run of 34 losses to the three-times world champions. They caught New Zealand cold with two early tries and two more at the start of the second half, and heroic Welsh defence resisted waves of attacks in the closing stages to hold on for a famous victory.  "It's come from belief. Obviously we've got the crowd behind us, and the energy and the noise was unbelievable," said Welsh man of the match James Botham.

"We've been training on the defensive side of things, and it shows how training has come on and just how much we have got each other's back." The Wales players team were in tears at the end amid raucous celebrations at the Principality Stadium after Tomos Williams, Dewi Lake, Archie Griffin, Eddie James and Louis Rees-Zammit scored tries and Sam Costelow was immaculate with the boot. New Zealand’s tries were scored by Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi, Fehi Fineanganofo and Peter Lakai, all converted by Richie Mo’unga. EARLY LEAD Home supporters were pinching themselves as Wales took less than 90 seconds to open the scoring and crossed the All Blacks' line for a second try five minutes later to move 14-0 ahead. Williams’ long pass to Rees-Zammit set up the first try with the winger kicking the ball ahead and the scrumhalf following up and being first to dive on the loose ball. Captain Lake scored the second try as he powered over from close range after Jac Morgan’s burst set up the opportunity. Although New Zealand got their first try when scrumhalf Ratima easily broke through the home defence in the 10th minute, the Welsh were in dreamland when they had a third try after battering away at the Kiwi line with tighthead prop Archie Griffin powering over. At halftime, however, the scores were level at 21-21 as New Zealand fought back with Sititi grabbing a try and winger Fineanganofo dotting down after a move started in his own half by Mo’unga and relentlessly driven forward to exhaust the Welsh defence. The All Blacks were expected to romp away in the second half but Wales scored two quick tries to again catch their visitors cold. After a series of carries through the middle, Williams’ long pass found James in the corner to score in the 44th minute. Five minutes later a drive from a lineout put Rees-Zammit over and gave Wales a 35-21 lead. Lakai reduced the deficit with a try to make 35-28 in the 53rd minute, after which the All Blacks camped on the Welsh line but were denied by stoic and lung-busting defence. Three times they were held up over the line with the Welsh defenders making a total of 346 tackles by the end of the game. It was only the fourth time Wales had beaten New Zealand in 39 meetings. "A hell of a defensive effort from them," New Zealand coach Dave Rennie said. "They were excellent tonight." One consolation for the All Blacks was that the bonus points they picked up put them above South Africa in the Northern Hemisphere standings as they seek a place in the new competition's final at Twickenham. (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

GENOA, Italy, Nov 14 : Italy came close but ultimately fell to another Nations Championship loss against Argentina on Saturday, with head coach Gonzalo Quesada left lamenting the errors and missed opportunities which cost his side. The final seconds of the match summed up Italy's afternoon in Genoa, putting themselves in a position to beat Argentina but letting the chance slip away in a 19-14 defeat. With the clock in the red, Italy were awarded a penalty. Paolo Garbisi went for touch in the corner, but the flyhalf overhit his kick and the Italians fell to a sixth consecutive defeat. Quesada's lineout coach, former Italy great Sergio Parisse, shook his head ruefully in the stands, and the two Argentine-born men looked increasingly frustrated throughout the match.

"Knowing that, after all the work we put in together during the week, we could have beaten Argentina with 30 seconds left, and that it was in our hands, hurts," Quesada told reporters. "We had the tools and the opportunity to win, but we let it slip away. We are still missing something, we need to be more solid." Italy failed to capitalise time and again on Argentine ill-discipline, with the Pumas having three players yellow carded. Captain Giacomo Nicotera believes their shortcomings extended beyond an inability to exploit numerical advantage. "It was a very messy game, with two teams going at each other with great intensity," Nicotera said. "My feeling is that even when the numbers were level, there were moments when we could have managed possession better, stayed organised and maintained control of the game, putting them under pressure. "That's something we'll have to review and analyse." This defeat will be one that haunts Quesada, and a loss he will certainly analyse before taking on Fiji next weekend. "I like the fact that the expectations around this team are that it should win," Quesada said. "I get angry when we give things away and those mistakes are entirely down to ourselves. "From where I sat, the feeling was that we could have controlled the game better and put them under pressure. It's one of those matches that I need to watch again before getting back to work."

LONDON, Nov 14 : Chelsea handed champions Manchester City their first defeat of the Women's Super League season on Saturday, beating their title rivals 1-0 to climb above them into top spot in the table. Chelsea have 26 points from 10 matches, one ahead of second-placed City after 10 games. The decisive moment came in first-half stoppage time when Sandy Baltimore produced a moment of brilliance, collecting a pass on the right side of the penalty area before turning and rifling an unstoppable shot above goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita. "I think just the intensity is a lot better," Chelsea midfielder Keira Walsh told the BBC. "And you could see today, I think we started a bit slow but after that most first and second balls were ours and I think that's what wins you games."

City's hopes of preserving their unbeaten record suffered a further blow in the 75th minute when Yamashita was sent off after racing well outside her area and clattering Alyssa Thompson as the Chelsea forward ran through on goal. Eartha Cumings replaced her as City played the closing stages with 10 players. Chelsea's Aggie Beever-Jones struck the crossbar with a free kick in the second half but the hosts held on for the victory. "I think (top spot) is kind of what Chelsea have been used to for so long but, yeah, it's a nice feeling," Walsh said. "We're in a better place than we were last year, it's a good feeling. We've got one more game before the international break, and we need to finish strong, but we're in a good place, we're confident, and the team's really happy." Chelsea next host Paris St Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday. Manchester United continued their solid start with a 2-0 victory over Crystal Palace with goals from captain Maya Le Tissier and Elisabeth Terland. Le Tissier celebrated her 150th United appearance in memorable fashion in the 18th minute, stepping out from defence to win possession before unleashing a superb long-range effort into the bottom corner of the net. United sealed the points in the 65th when Jess Park collected her second assist of the afternoon, threading a precise pass into the box for Terland, who calmly beat the goalkeeper for her third WSL goal of the season. The win leaves United provisionally fourth on 18 points. Tottenham Hotspur are fifth after a 0-0 draw with Everton, who are seventh. And Liverpool leapfrogged Brighton & Hove Albion into eighth place after a 3-0 victory, with Beata Olsson scoring in each half, and Cornelia Kapocs bagging the Reds' other goal. Brighton are ninth and trail Liverpool only on goal difference.

GENOA, Italy, Nov 14 : Argentina beat Italy 19-14 on Saturday in a Nations Championship meeting short on quality and high on errors which condemned the hosts to their fifth defeat in five matches in the competition. Italy took an early lead through Monty Ioane's try, converted by Tommaso Allan, but Argentina, who were down to 14 men, levelled just before halftime, with hooker Bautista Bernasconi going over and Tomas Albornoz adding the conversion. Rodrigo Isgro's try in the 55th minute put Argentina ahead and five minutes later Mateo Carreras extended the lead when he went over for the visitors, with Albornoz converting. A penalty try for Italy set up a grandstand finish but Argentina held on for their 10th straight win over the Italians.

Argentina earned their second victory of the competition and are on 11 points, third in the Southern Hemisphere standings, three points ahead of Australia, who visit Scotland on Sunday. Italy earned a losing bonus point, their first of the competition, but will finish bottom of the Northern Hemisphere group. Both sides came into the contest low on confidence and in need of not only victory, but a much-improved performance. Argentina lost 42-12 to Ireland a week ago, while Italy were thumped 66-7 by South Africa in Turin. BRIGHT START The Italian fans suffered through a dominant Springbok performance last week, especially a first half which was all one-way traffic, but this time around the hosts started brightly in Genoa with a fifth-minute try. Leonardo Marin's kick through on the wing bounced up perfectly for Ioane to go over in the corner. That move followed an Italian penalty won at the scrum, and Argentina were penalised twice more in the first half for collapsing. Allan missed a penalty from inside his own half, and Italy continually failed to capitalise on Argentine ill-discipline. After kicking two penalties into the corner, Italy lost their lineout close to the line. Albornoz was sent to the sin-bin just before the half-hour mark but Argentina then had their best spell and Bernasconi's try from a lineout drive was converted by the flyhalf, back on the pitch just in time for the kick. Argentina continued to make plenty of entries into the Italian 22 after the break, but errors let them down until they managed to hold firm in the scrum and worked the ball to the other side for Isgro to put them ahead. Italy lost Enoch Opoku Gyamfi to a yellow card for too many penalties and Argentina pounced immediately with Carreras' try. Argentina's Joel Sclavi was yellow carded, and Efrain Elias quickly followed suit when Italy were awarded a penalty try with 15 minutes remaining but their late pressure went unrewarded. Gonzalo Quesada's Italy will hope to finish off in style next Saturday when they host Fiji in Udine, the only other winless side in the competition, and the pair are likely to meet on finals weekend in the 11th-place final. Argentina travel to Paris next weekend to take on France, who top the Northern Hemisphere standings.

LEVI, Finland, Nov 14 : Germany's Emma Aicher claimed the first women's World Cup slalom of the season on Saturday, turning her opening-run lead into a dominant victory to secure the first slalom win of her career. Aicher, who turned 23 on Friday, had a 0.36-second advantage after the first run and looked comfortable in extending her advantage in the second run on the Levi Black course to finish with a combined time of one minute 52.62 seconds. She finished 0.43 seconds ahead of Albania's Lara Colturi, while Austria's Katharina Truppe climbed from fifth after the first run to complete the podium, 0.50 behind the winner. The victory adds slalom to Aicher's growing World Cup resume after previous wins in downhill and super-G.

"It's a good birthday present," Aicher said. "I like Levi, it was my first (slalom) podium (last year), first win in slalom (this year), so it means a lot to be here. My whole family is here as well, so it's really nice to be able to ski the way I want when they are here. "I'm happy with how I skied in both rounds. There's still a few things I could do better but, overall, I'm happy." Colturi, 19, made the ninth World Cup podium of her career but is still searching for her first World Cup win. Croatia's Zrinka Ljutic, third after the opening run, slipped to fourth. Another major storyline was the return to the discipline of Slovakia's 31-year-old Petra Vlhova, who finished 16th in her first World Cup slalom since January 2024. The six-times Levi winner qualified for the second run in 14th place and showed flashes of her former speed. Vlhova, who came back to the World Cup circuit in the giant slalom at Solden last month, was seriously injured in January 2024 when she fell in that event on home snow in Jasna and tore knee ligaments. She underwent two surgical operations. The season-opening slalom was contested without reigning discipline champion Mikaela Shiffrin, who won nine of the 10 World Cup slaloms last winter. The American plans to begin her slalom campaign at Killington on November 29. Winners of the Levi races receive a live Lapland reindeer as part of their prize, a tradition started in 2013.

MILAN: Italy's data protection agency said on Saturday (Nov 14) it had fined Meta Platforms €805 million (US$887 million) after finding the company had accessed Android users' photographs and videos without obtaining their consent or informing them. Meta had access to Android users' photos and videos through a Facebook app feature that suggested content from users' personal galleries that they could post, the authority said in a statement. Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately, it said. A Meta spokesperson said the company would appeal, strongly disagreeing with the authority's decision and calling the fine "disproportionate".

Users must grant permission on their device before the feature can operate, and they can change that permission at any time in their settings," the spokesperson said in a statement. The investigation, which began in 2025, did not cover the possible use of the content to train artificial intelligence models, a practice Meta denied, the authority said. The authority also said that it had reserved the right to assess separately a new feature, launched in 2026, that allows content from users' galleries to be processed in the cloud. The fine is equivalent to about 0.47 percent of the group's global revenue, the authority said. Around 20 million Android users in Italy have been affected, it said.

ASEAN not easing Myanmar approach, bloc's special envoy says

ASEAN special envoy and Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro says the grouping is not relaxing its approach to Myanmar under its Five-Point Consensus.

Philippine Foreign Secretary Maria Theresa lazaro (centre) delivers her opening statement during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Foreign Ministers’ meeting in Manila on Nov 14, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Pool/Jam Sta Rosa)

MANILA: ASEAN is not relaxing its approach to Myanmar under its Five-Point Consensus, though proposals concerning the country's participation in high-level meetings remain under discussion, the bloc's special envoy on Myanmar said on Saturday (Nov 14). The Five-Point Consensus is ASEAN's main framework for responding to the crisis in Myanmar after a military coup there in 2021. It calls, among other things, for an immediate end to violence and the launch of constructive dialogue among all parties, and offers ASEAN mediation and humanitarian assistance. ASEAN is under increasing pressure ahead of a summit of its leaders in Manila that starts on Sunday to ease a five-year ban on Myanmar's military-backed leaders attending high-level meetings. Thailand and several other members have stepped up engagement with Myanmar despite its ongoing civil war. ASEAN special envoy and Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Maria Theresa Lazaro said a draft review of the Five-Point Consensus was still under negotiation and that "a number of proposals" would be presented to the ASEAN leaders.

"To answer you bluntly, there is no easing (of the approach to Myanmar). There is still the Five-Point Consensus," Lazaro told a press conference, when asked whether the review could lead to adjustments to restrictions on Myanmar's political leadership.

ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus

Following a 2021 military coup , ASEAN has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings as it has yet to make meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities.  During a meeting in April 2021, all ASEAN leaders reached a consensus about the situation in Myanmar. The five points are: First, there shall be immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar and all parties shall exercise utmost restraint. Second, constructive dialogue among all parties concerned shall commence to seek a peaceful solution in the interests of the people. Third, a special envoy of the ASEAN chair shall facilitate mediation of the dialogue process, with the assistance of the secretary-general of ASEAN. Fourth, ASEAN shall provide humanitarian assistance through the AHA Centre. Fifth, the special envoy and delegation shall visit Myanmar to meet with all parties concerned.

Collapse Expand

Asked about Thailand's call to allow Myanmar's foreign minister to participate in meetings of ASEAN foreign ministers, Lazaro said it remained under discussion, but no decision had been made to allow the minister to take Myanmar's seat. "It's still there on the table. It's still a subject of discussion," she said. Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations are set to review their decision to exclude Myanmar when they meet in Manila from Nov 15 to Nov 17.
